whatIs.title: What are PDF Tools?
whatIs.description: Merge PDFs, split or extract pages, delete/rotate/reorder pages, and convert images (JPG, PNG) to PDF on one screen. Most online PDF sites upload your file to a server; this tool processes it inside your browser, so the file never leaves your device.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Merge: add several PDFs, set the order by dragging (or with the up/down buttons), then press "Merge PDFs". The result is saved as "firstfile_merged.pdf".
Split: add one PDF and pick a method. For a range type "1-3, 5, 8-" (8- = page 8 to the end); "Every N pages" and "Each page" download several files as one ZIP.

Organize pages: undo or redo up to 30 moves, rotations, deletions and full resets. Save changes uses the edits captured at the click; later edits or tab changes prevent the old result from being applied.
Image→PDF: add photos and choose the paper (A4, Letter, original size), orientation and margin. Each image becomes one page.

tips.title: Tips
items: Scans named scan_1, scan_2… can be put in order at once with "Sort by name" (numbers sorted numerically).
To get each range as its own file, turn on "Save each range as a separate file" under Split → Page Range.
Phone photos that used to come out sideways are straightened automatically using their EXIF orientation.
Merge, split and organize copy the original pages as-is, so text and image quality are unchanged.

items.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
items.a: No. Files are read and processed only in this browser's memory and are never sent to any server. They disappear when you close the page.
PDFs with an open password or editing restrictions cannot be processed. Open the file in a PDF viewer with the password and save a copy with "Print to PDF", then use that copy.

items.q: Is there a file size limit?
items.a: There is no fixed limit, but processing uses browser memory, so files of several hundred MB may be slow or fail. A desktop can handle larger files than a phone.

Merge, split and organize copy pages without re-rendering, so quality is unchanged. Image→PDF embeds JPG and PNG originals as-is; only photos that need orientation correction and WebP/GIF images are re-saved as high-quality JPG.
It changes the page rotation value in the PDF, so the content is untouched and other PDF viewers show the same orientation.

items.q: Can I convert PDF to JPG?
items.a: Only image→PDF is supported at the moment.

history.title: Page edit history
history.count: {undo} undo steps · {redo} redo steps · Up to {max} steps
history.hint: Undo page moves, rotation, deletion and restoring the original layout. Use Ctrl/⌘+Z to undo and Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Z to redo. Editing inside an input keeps its native undo behavior.
history.undone: Returned to the previous page edit.
history.replaced: Opened the new PDF and started a new edit history.
history.replaceHint: The current document is replaced only after the new PDF loads successfully. A failed read keeps your current edits.
history.memoryOnly: Edit history lasts only while you use this page. Original file bytes are not copied for each history step or saved.
history.snapshot: Export uses the files and edit order captured when you press the button. Later edits or tab changes cancel the previous operation's result display and automatic download.
history.invalidated: Inputs changed, so the previous result was cleared. Export the current edits again.
